eventMetadata.context_description: Hong Kong Observatory's latest 9-day forecast, issued around May 6, projects a high of 22–25°C on May 9 amid a strengthening northeast monsoon bringing showers and squally thunderstorms from an approaching trough of low pressure over southern China. This follows May 6's confirmed peak of 24.2°C under persistent cloud cover, well below May's typical 28–29°C average high, as moderating monsoon winds limit solar heating and upper-air disturbances suppress temperatures. Trader consensus reflects tight uncertainty around 24–27°C, hinging on cloud break timing and monsoon surge strength—persistent overcast favors 22–24°C, while afternoon clearing could push toward 26–27°C— with new HKO updates expected twice daily resolving key variables before the weekend.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket reflects tight uncertainty in short-range forecasts for Shanghai's May 9 high temperature, with models clustering around 22–25°C amid typical early-May climatology averaging 23°C daily maximums at the official Pudong station. Urban heat island effects add ~1–2°C, while sea breezes could temper extremes; China Meteorological Administration updates tomorrow may refine odds before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: PAGASA's latest 5-day outlook for Port Area in Metro Manila forecasts a 34-35°C high on May 9 amid partly cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms from easterlies, driving trader consensus to tightly cluster implied probabilities around 34-37°C at 25-27% each. Recent observations underscore this uncertainty: Science Garden in Quezon City hit 35.5°C and NAIA Pasay reached 36.3°C on May 6 during the ongoing dry-season heatwave, where urban heat island effects amplify actual air temperatures beyond averages of 33-34°C for May. Differentiating factors include potential sea breeze moderation versus prolonged sunshine boosting peaks to 37°C, with daily PAGASA updates and new model runs expected to refine guidance ahead of resolution based on the official station reading.
